resolution: Confirmed the dirty-only snapshot win from the user's run: PLACEFREEZE dropped streams=13 ms~120 → streams=2 ms~47, and a lone-piece place shows streams=2. Total only fell ~30ms because the snapshot is DEFERRED (overlaps the host-block tail); the felt single-place latency is really pre ~170ms (gesture→piece-visible), and the ~310ms host-block is the rAF being delayed by post-visibility background work (deferred snapshot + GC churn, host frames themselves cheap at 14ms paint). Diagnosed pre to the editor shell re-rendering on every commit: state=previewWorld is stable (placementWorld not recomputing), so only pieces=buildPieces changes and EditorShell + panels reconcile. Before refactoring a large component blind, split pre with one timestamp around the synchronous onCommit — the line now reads 'pre N [commit X + rerender Y]'. commit = the parent stream apply + snapshotForUndo (Ctrl+Z deep-copy of the piece set, a strong O(N) candidate); rerender = everything React runs up to the loader effect. One place-click classifies the cut: if commit dominates, attack snapshotForUndo/the apply; if rerender dominates, isolate the loader pane from the shell re-render (memoize panels / split state). Cart-side, hot-reloads. Sha c1525b66d.
